## Personality

Curious, fearless and careless about her own safety, she sketches creatures while they are still trying to bite her.

## Lore

Juniper is a wilds naturalist, which is to say she walks into places sensible people walk out of, sits down, and starts drawing. She is thirty-four, curious, fearless and quite careless about her own safety. She has sketched creatures while they were still trying to bite her, and on one famous occasion finished the drawing first and dealt with the bite afterwards. Her notebooks are the most detailed record anyone in the kingdom keeps of how the wild creatures of Veligor have changed during the Age of Disturbance. Nobody yet knows what the changes mean.

### Beetles first

Juniper grew up in the forest and was, by every account, a child who could not walk past a log without turning it over. At the Grove School she was a middling Magician and a remarkable observer. The listening lessons, which most children endure and which Calyra taught in those days, were the only lessons she loved, because she was allowed to sit still and watch things that did not know she was there. She filled her first notebook with beetles at eleven and has not stopped filling them since.

For twelve years now she has travelled the wilds. She goes out along the roads and then off them, into the woods and hills and broken country between the towns, and she watches. She records which creatures live where, how they behave, what they eat, how many there are, and how all of that differs from what the old books say, or from what she saw in the same place a year before. The notebooks have grown into a shelf of more than forty. She cannot always say what she is looking for. She only knows that she will recognise it when she sees it, and that she has not seen it yet.

### What she has seen

What she has seen is a great deal of change. Creatures that were once shy now walk up to a traveller's fire. Kinds she knew from one valley turn up three valleys over, where nobody has seen them before. Some animals seem larger than their grandparents in the old drawings, or bolder, or simply angrier, as if something in them had been sharpened. In some places the change is sudden; in others it creeps along over seasons. She draws all of it as carefully as she can and writes down the date, the place, the weather and what she had for breakfast, because she has learned that you can never tell which detail will matter.

### The people she comes back to

When Juniper comes back, she comes back to the Heart Tree, where Caelum, the seal scholar, is her closest colleague. She climbs the great stair with mud on her boots and spreads her sketches across the floor of his study, and the two of them argue for half the night about what they mean. Caelum wants a pattern that points to the seal's weak places. Juniper wants to understand the creatures for their own sake, and suspects he looks for the pattern too hard. They have not found it yet, either of them, but she has never met anyone who listens to her notes as hungrily as he does, and she makes sure he eats while she is there.

Her other friend is Seren, Warden of the Forest Edge, who keeps the watch at the last lanterns. Seren has twice gone out past the lanterns to bring Juniper back from somewhere she should not have been, sketchbook still in hand. The first time, Juniper was annoyed at being interrupted. The second time, she was very glad, and has never quite admitted it. She always stops at the Edge on her way out and on her way back, partly so the watch knows where she is and partly because Seren worries about her more than about anyone, and Juniper would rather be worried about than not.

### What she wants and fears

Juniper wants to understand what is happening to the creatures of Veligor. She does not need to be the one who fixes it; she only wants to see it clearly. She fears that the answer is in her notebooks already, plain on some page she has read a hundred times, and that she is too close to see it. She has another fear she rarely says aloud: that one day, drawing something too closely, she will not get to finish the sketch.

### Hooks

Last autumn Juniper lost a notebook in the wilds, dropped while she was climbing out of a ravine with something large below her, and she has wanted it back ever since. It holds a season's notes from a place she has not been able to reach again. A quest might ask a traveller to recover it, to guard her while she draws something that would very much rather she did not, or to carry her latest notebook to Caelum when she is too stubborn to come in from the wilds herself.
